questions.question: In March 2025, the Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill 2024 was passed in the Lok Sabha. This bill seeks to amend which of the following Acts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Disaster Management Act, 2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill, 2024** was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **August 1, 2024**, and subsequently passed in **March 2025** to amend the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**.
 
• The primary objective of the amendment is to bring more **clarity and convergence** in the roles of various authorities working in the field of disaster management at the **National** and **State** levels.
 
• One of the significant features of the Bill is the establishment of a **National Disaster Database**, which will be maintained at the national level to store critical information related to disaster risks and mitigation.
 
• The Bill provides for the constitution of **Urban Disaster Management Authorities** in state capitals and large cities with **Municipal Corporations**, acknowledging the unique challenges of urban flooding and infrastructure risks.
 
• It grants **statutory recognition** to existing bodies such as the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** and the **State Disaster Response Force (SDRF)**, formalizing their roles and responsibilities within the legal framework.
 
• The amendment empowers the **Central Government** to make regulations concerning the **Disaster Management** framework, ensuring a more flexible and responsive system to modern-day calamities. ***Hence, the correct answer is The Disaster Management Act, 2005.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Disaster Management Act, 2005**:
 
 
• This Act was enacted by the **Parliament of India** on **December 23, 2005**, following the devastating **2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami**.
 
• It established a three-tier structure: the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** at the center, the **State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)** at the state level, and the **District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)** at the district level.
 
• The **Prime Minister of India** serves as the ex-officio **Chairperson** of the **NDMA**, while the **Chief Ministers** lead the respective **SDMAs**.
 
 
 
• **Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897**:
 
 
• This is a colonial-era law meant to provide for the better prevention of the spread of dangerous epidemic diseases. It was widely invoked during the **COVID-19 pandemic** in **2020**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Protection Act, 1986**:
 
 
• Enacted in the wake of the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy**, this Act empowers the **Central Government** to protect and improve environmental quality and control pollution.
 
 
 
• **National Green Tribunal Act, 2010**:
 
 
• This Act enabled the creation of the **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to **environmental protection** and conservation of forests.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Revisions in 2024 Bill**:
 
 
• The **2024 Bill** seeks to address the "overlapping" of functions between the **NDMA** and various ministries, ensuring that the **National Plan** is more comprehensive.
 
• It introduces provisions for **financial penalties** for individuals or organizations that fail to comply with the directions issued by the **Central** or **State Governments** regarding disaster management.
 
• The creation of the **National Disaster Database** is expected to help in **evidence-based decision-making** by tracking the **allocation and utilization** of funds from the **National Disaster Response Fund**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: On 1 September 2025, the rupee ___________ to a record low before recovering after likely RBI intervention.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fell to ₹88.33 per USD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **1 September 2025**, the **Indian Rupee** experienced significant selling pressure, causing it to breach a new historic low of **₹88.33** against the **US Dollar**.
 
• The primary drivers for this depreciation included a strengthening **US Dollar Index (DXY)** and consistent **Foreign Institutional Investor (FII)** outflows from the **Indian capital markets**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the fall to 88.33 is correct.***
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** reportedly intervened in the **Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF)** and spot markets by selling **US Dollars** through **public sector banks** to provide support to the local currency.
 
• Global economic factors, such as high **crude oil prices** and rising **US Treasury yields**, contributed to the rupee's vulnerability, as India is a major importer of energy.
 
• The intervention by the central bank was aimed at curbing **excessive volatility** rather than targeting a specific exchange rate level, allowing the rupee to recover slightly after hitting the record low.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Currency Depreciation:**
 
 
• This is the fall in the value of a currency in a **floating exchange rate system** due to market forces like **demand and supply**.
 
• A weaker rupee makes **exports more competitive** but increases the cost of **imports**, leading to **imported inflation** in the domestic economy.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**
 
 
• The **RBI** manages the exchange rate through its **Foreign Exchange Reserves**, which include **Foreign Currency Assets (FCA)**, **Gold**, **Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)**, and the **Reserve Position in the IMF**.
 
• In **2024-2025**, India’s **Forex Reserves** have been maintained at high levels to shield the economy from **external shocks** and speculative attacks on the currency.
 
 
 
• **External Factors:**
 
 
• The **monetary policy** of the **US Federal Reserve** plays a crucial role; when the **Fed** raises interest rates, capital often flows back to the **United States**, weakening currencies in **Emerging Markets** like **India**.
 
• The **Current Account Deficit (CAD)** is also a vital indicator; a widening deficit puts structural pressure on the **rupee's value** over the long term.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Exchange Rate Management:** Unlike a fixed regime, India follows a **managed float** system where the market determines the rate, but the **RBI** steps in to prevent **wild fluctuations**.
 
• **Impact on Sectors:**
 
 
• **Beneficiaries:** **IT services**, **textiles**, and **pharmaceuticals** often benefit from a weaker rupee as their **dollar-denominated earnings** translate into more rupees.
 
• **Losers:** **Oil marketing companies**, **importers of electronics**, and **students studying abroad** face higher costs when the rupee falls to record lows like **88.33**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:** The rupee has seen a gradual depreciation over the decades, moving from around **₹4.76** in **1947** to over **₹80** in **2022**, and reaching the **₹88** mark in late **2025**.

__
 
• On **26 May 2025**, the **NITI Aayog** released a landmark report titled **'Designing a Policy for Medium Enterprises'**, which outlines a strategic framework to bolster the growth of the **MSME** sector. ***Hence, the correct answer is NITI Aayog.***
 
• The report identifies **Medium Enterprises** as the "missing middle" in India's industrial landscape and proposes a dedicated roadmap to transform them into globally competitive **growth engines**.
 
• Key recommendations in the report focus on **Ease of Doing Business (EoDB)**, providing better **access to credit**, and facilitating **technological upgrades** for firms that have graduated from being small-scale units.
 
• The document emphasizes the need for **structural reforms** to help these enterprises integrate into **Global Value Chains (GVCs)**, thereby contributing significantly to India's goal of becoming a **USD 5 trillion economy**.
 
• It suggests the creation of **sector-specific clusters** and specialized **Export Promotion Cells** to assist **Medium Enterprises** in expanding their footprint in international markets.

• It provides employment to over **11 crore people** across the country, making it the second-largest employer after **agriculture**.
 
• Schemes like **Udyam Registration**, the **RAMP (Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance)** program, and the **Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS)** are designed to support this vital sector.

• The **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** facilitates capital raising for smaller firms through **SME Exchanges** like **NSE Emerge** and **BSE SME**.

• **One Vehicle, One FASTag Initiative:**
 
 
• Launched by **NHAI** in **2024**, this initiative aims to discourage the use of a single **FASTag** for multiple vehicles or linking multiple **FASTags** to a single vehicle.
 
• It enhances the efficiency of **Electronic Toll Collection (ETC)** and ensures that the vehicle class registered matches the physical vehicle passing through the **toll lane**.
